problem: The graph of the function $f(x)$ passes through $(3,-1)$ and ${f}^{′}(3)=2.$ Find $L(x)$, the tangent line approximation of $f(x)$ at $x=3.$

activity_context.topic_title: Approximating Functions Using Local Linearity and Linearization

examples.knowledge_point: Estimating the Value of a Function at a Point Using a Tangent Line Approximation
examples.problem: Suppose that $f(-2) = 0$ and $f'(-2)=2.$ Estimate the value of $f(-1.8)$ using the tangent line approximation of $f(x)$ at $x=-2.$
examples.worked_solution:
The tangent line approximation to $f(x)$ at the point $a=-2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}L(x) & =f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a) \\  & =f(-2)+{f}^{′}(-2)(x-(-2)) \\  & =0+2(x+2) \\  & =2(x+2).\end{aligned}
$$

We can approximate $f(-1.8)$ by evaluating the tangent line approximation at $x=-1.8.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-1.8) & ≈L(-1.8) \\  & =2(-1.8+2) \\  & =2(0.2) \\  & =0.4.\end{aligned}
$$
